# Color

The decisions behind this page are architecture decision records: see [Decisions](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/decisions-all-decisions--overview.md).

Every swatch on this page is painted from the live CSS variable, split down the middle into the
light and dark theme, and labelled with the value and ratio **computed from `tokens.css`** by the
resolver the contract test uses. If a label disagreed with its paint, the build would already be
red.

## Cloth — the grounds

Bleached cotton in the light theme; the dyed base layer in the dark one. `cloth-pale` is *raised*
in both themes — lighter on light, lighter on dark — so "raised" means the same thing either way.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--cloth` | The page. | `#edeee8` | `#16181c` |
| `--cloth-pale` | Raised: cards, inputs, menus, dialogs. | `#f6f7f2` | `#1e2126` |
| `--cloth-shade` | One step down: table headers, wells, disabled fields. | `#e4e7dc` | `#111316` |
| `--cloth-deep` | The deepest cloth before a layer takes over. | `#d7dbcb` | `#2a2e34` |

## Ink — the top layer

The foreground, and every keyline. `--ink` keeps its *role* across themes, not its hue.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ink` | Body text, headings, every interactive edge. | `#14161a` | `#eceee6` |
| `--ink-2` | Secondary text. | `#3d4147` | `#c4c8bd` |
| `--ink-muted` | Tertiary text, metadata. Floor of the ramp. | `#5e636a` | `#9a9f97` |
| `--keyline` | Decorative dividers only. Under 3:1 on purpose. | `#c6cabc` | `#3a3f46` |

## The four layers

Commercial cotton in the range a mola is actually cut from. Flat, saturated, never mixed with each
other. In the dark theme they are lifted until they carry text on the dark ground.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--rojo` | Danger, through the danger role, on a product screen. The editorial accent in Prose. | `#c0272d` | `#f2685c` |
| `--anil` | Information, links in tools, selection. | `#1b4b8f` | `#86a8ee` |
| `--verde` | Success, healthy, approved. | `#0b6b4b` | `#4cc493` |
| `--oro` | The accent: the revealed band. A field and a mark — never text on light cloth. | `#edb01f` | `#f0bc3a` |

## Washes

A mola has no tints, so washes are reserved for a whole region that belongs to a layer without
becoming it: a callout, a selected row, a running step. Mixed thin enough that **every step of the
ink ramp stays legal on every wash**.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--rojo-soft` | Danger callout, failed step. | `#f3e0d9` | `#352a2d` |
| `--anil-soft` | Info callout, selected row, uncertainty note. | `#dae2e7` | `#292f3b` |
| `--verde-soft` | Success callout. | `#dce6dc` | `#253232` |
| `--oro-soft` | Highlight, waiting-for-approval. | `#f5ead0` | `#302f2c` |
| `--ink-soft` | Hover on ghost controls, inline code ground. | `#e4e5e1` | `#2a2d31` |

## Roles: danger, accent, selection

A layer says what a thing is made of; a role says what it means. Components use the role, so the
meaning is in the code and an app can re-dye a role without repainting a layer. **On a product
screen rojo is used only through the danger role**: a red rótulo band, list marker or agent name
beside a red FAILED mark made the failure one red thing among several
([ADR 0008](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/?path=/docs/decisions-0008-the-rojo-register--overview)). The
editorial accent (rojo links and list markers in `Prose`) is the one exception, and a test holds
the components to it.

| Token | Role | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--danger` | A failed or destructive thing: a status mark, a bar, the danger button’s fill. | `#c0272d` | `#f2685c` |
| `--danger-strong` | The danger button, pressed. | `#9e1e24` | `#ff8a7e` |
| `--danger-soft` | A region that belongs to a failure: an error callout, a failed tool call. | `#f3e0d9` | `#352a2d` |
| `--accent` | The band a control reveals, the working texture, selected text. | `#edb01f` | `#f0bc3a` |
| `--accent-soft` | A region that belongs to the accent. | `#f5ead0` | `#302f2c` |
| `--selected` | An item chosen for an action: a selected row, the bulk-action bar. | `#f5ead0` | `#302f2c` |

Real text on real grounds, in both themes. 4.5 is the bar for text, 3 for a UI boundary.

| `--ink` | `--cloth` | 15.52 | 15.18 |
| `--ink-muted` | `--cloth-shade` | 4.83 | 6.89 |
| `--ink-muted` | `--oro-soft` | 5.05 | 4.98 |
| `--rojo` | `--cloth` | 5.04 | 5.85 |
| `--warn` | `--cloth` | 4.60 | 9.18 |
| `--on-layer` | `--danger` | 5.46 | 5.31 |
| `--ink-danger` | `--danger-soft` | 6.19 | 6.02 |
| `--on-accent` | `--accent` | 9.34 | 9.19 |
| `--ink-muted` | `--selected` | 5.05 | 4.98 |
| `--on-layer` | `--anil` | 7.96 | 6.80 |
| `--on-layer` | `--verde` | 6.06 | 7.40 |
| `--on-oro` | `--oro` | 9.34 | 9.19 |
| `--on-ink` | `--ink` | 16.82 | 13.79 |
| `--on-ink-muted` | `--ink` | 8.36 | 6.56 |

Those are a sample. The full list, every pairing the contract test measures, is published with
each token in the agent docs (`llms-tokens.txt`, `get_tokens` on the MCP server) as the grounds it
reads `on` and the foregrounds it carries `under`. A pairing not on that list was never measured.

## Scopes: what each colour is for

Tailwind generates every colour utility for every token, so `text-cloth-pale` compiles as readily
as `bg-cloth-pale`. Only one of them was measured. Each colour token is therefore scoped to the jobs
it does, from five: a **surface** carries content, **text** colours words, an **edge** is a line, a
**mark** is a small graphic that is not a region, and an **overlay** sits over content the system
cannot know. A token can have several: rojo fills a panel, reads as text on cloth, keys a swatch
and is a cut band. Gold has no text scope, because it fails on light cloth; the status tones have
none either, because words in a status take `--ink-danger` and its kin, which `on-layer` collapses
on a filled panel.

| Scope | What it is | Tailwind | Figma |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `surface` | A ground that carries content: a page, a panel, a card, a wash, a filled layer. | `bg-` | `FRAME_FILL` `SHAPE_FILL` |
| `text` | The colour of words, and of icons that inherit `currentColor`. | `text-` `placeholder-` `caret-` | `TEXT_FILL` |
| `edge` | A line: a keyline, a divider, an underline, a current-item bar, the revealed band of a cut. Mola draws most edges with `box-shadow`. | `border-` `border-x-` `border-y-` `border-t-` `border-b-` `border-s-` `border-e-` `border-l-` `border-r-` `divide-` `outline-` `ring-` `decoration-` `stroke-` `cut-` `bar-start-` `bar-bottom-` | `STROKE_COLOR` `EFFECT_COLOR` |
| `mark` | A small filled graphic that is not a region: a status dot, a swatch key, a switch thumb, a rule drawn as a 1px box. | `bg-` `fill-` `stroke-` | `SHAPE_FILL` |
| `overlay` | A translucent fill over content the system cannot know: a scrim over an image, the backdrop behind a modal. | `bg-` | `FRAME_FILL` `SHAPE_FILL` |

A test reads every component and pattern and fails on a colour utility outside its token's scope,
and fails if a promised pairing puts a token in a role its scope does not allow. The agent docs list
each token's valid utilities, and `tokens/mola.tokens.json` carries the same scopes as Figma
variable scopes (`com.figma.scopes`) with the CSS variable as code syntax, so a Figma kit built from
it offers a surface only as a fill.

## Two themes, one declaration

```css
--cloth: light-dark(#edeee8, #16181c);
```

Each token is written once with both values, and `color-scheme` picks one. That buys three things
a duplicated `[data-theme=dark]` block does not: the OS preference is honoured with no script, any
subtree can flip theme on its own, and a token cannot exist in one theme and be forgotten in the
other.

The colour tokens are declared on `:root` and again on every `[data-theme]` element. A browser
that reads `light-dark()` natively doesn't need the second one. A production build does: Lightning
CSS rewrites `light-dark()` for older browsers into custom properties, and those resolve where the
token is declared, not where it is used. With the tokens on `:root` alone, a dark panel inside a
light page would paint light. The browser audit checks that every `data-theme` subtree paints its
own ground, and the light and dark halves of the swatches on this page are two such subtrees.
